content:
Dating reality shows have long been a popular genre, but Apple TV+ has never ventured into this space. While its newly announced series "The Last Person on Earth" is positioned as a "documentary series" rather than a "reality show," it is still the streaming platform's first dating program.

"The Last Person on Earth" is hosted by renowned relationship therapist Esther Perel and has been described as an "innovative experiment."

Esther Perel is a famous relationship therapist and New York Times bestselling author who specializes in the field of interpersonal relationships.

Perel is also the central figure in Apple TV+'s newly announced eight-episode dating documentary series "The Last Person on Earth."

The press release states: "In this show, seemingly mismatched couples will be carefully matched by Perel and a team of matchmaking experts and therapists, before embarking on a journey to the world's most romantic and remote destinations."

It sounds very much like a reality show, but without the negative baggage associated with the "reality" brand. I suspect Apple is trying to create a sense of "elevation" for the dating show format, hence labeling it a "documentary series."

Incidentally, Apple also announced yesterday that it will adapt bestselling novelist Rebecca Yarros's latest romance novel into a TV series. Clearly, the streaming platform is looking to break out of its current core genres of sci-fi, comedy, and thriller, and venture into new territory.

Apple TV+ costs US$12.99 per month, with discounts available through the Apple One bundle.
